sentences: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain’s National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well.
DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world.
The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants.

It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1. 6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy.
translations: 任何对英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）与DeepMind之间交易危险性的公正评估，都必须首先承认双方都是出于好意。
DeepMind是全球领先的人工智能（AI）公司之一。
这项工作应用于医疗保健领域的潜力巨大，但也可能导致权力进一步集中在科技巨头手中。
正是在这种背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对NHS下属的皇家自由医院信托基金做出了严厉的裁决，该信托基金在2015年基于一项模糊的协议，将160万患者的记录交给了DeepMind，而该协议对患者的权利及其隐私期望考虑得太少。

sentences: DeepMind has almost apologised.
The NHS trust has mended its ways.

Further arrangements—and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned.
There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn.
But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important.
Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it “controlled” the data and DeepMind merely “processed” it.
But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.
translations: DeepMind几乎已经道歉了。
NHS信托基金已经改正了其做法。
NHS与DeepMind之间的进一步安排——可能还会有很多——将受到仔细审查，以确保已向患者征求所有必要的许可，并且所有不必要的数据已被清除。
在患者知情同意方面有经验教训需要吸取。
但隐私并不是本案中唯一的视角，甚至不是最重要的。
德纳姆女士选择将责任集中在NHS信托基金上，因为根据现行法律，它“控制”了数据，而DeepMind只是“处理”了数据。
但这种区分忽略了一个关键点：正是处理和聚合，而非仅仅拥有数据位，才赋予了数据价值。

sentences: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate.
Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them.
That misses the way the surveillance economy works.
The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
translations: 最大的问题是，谁应该从对我们现在生活所产生的所有数据的分析中受益。
隐私法建立在可识别个人知识对其造成损害的概念之上。
这忽略了监控经济的运作方式。
在那里，个人的数据只有与无数其他人的数据进行比较时才能获得其价值。

sentences: The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted.
This practice does not address the real worry.
It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives.
What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources.
If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as big pharma has done.
We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later.
A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism.
Ms Denham’s report is a welcome start.
translations: 在这种情况下，利用隐私法来约束科技巨头感觉有些不太适应。
这种做法并没有解决真正的担忧。
仅仅说DeepMind开发的算法将使患者受益并拯救生命是不够的。
重要的是，它们将属于一个利用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。
如果软件承诺能像现在的药物那样大规模拯救生命，那么大数据可能会像大型制药公司那样行事。
我们仍处于这场革命的初期，现在的小选择日后可能会产生巨大的后果。
要避免数字封建主义的未来，需要进行长期的斗争。
德纳姆女士的报告是一个受欢迎的起点。

sentences:
31. What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?
A. It fell short of the latter’s expectations.
B. It caused conflicts among tech giants.
C. It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.
D. It put both sides into a dangerous situation.
translations:
31. 关于NHS与DeepMind之间的协议，以下哪项说法是正确的？
A. 它未达到后者的期望。
B. 它引发了科技巨头之间的冲突。
C. 它未能充分关注患者的权利。
D. 它将双方置于危险的境地。

sentences:
32. The NHS trust responded to Denham’s verdict with
A. empty promises.
B. tough resistance.
C. sincere apologies.
D. necessary adjustments.
translations:
32. 英国国家医疗服务体系信托基金对德纳姆的裁决作出的回应是
A. 空洞的承诺。
B. 强硬的抵制。
C. 真诚的道歉。
D. 必要的调整。

sentences:
33. The author argues in Paragraph 2 that
A. privacy protection must be secured at all costs.
B. the value of data comes from the processing of it.
C. making profits from patients’ data is illegal.
D. leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it.
translations:
33. 作者在第二段中论证道
A. 隐私保护必须不惜一切代价加以确保。
B. 数据的价值来源于对其的处理。
C. 从患者数据中获利是非法的。
D. 泄露患者数据比出售它更糟糕。

sentences:
34. 3s.
According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is
A. the monopoly of big data by tech giants.
B. the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.
C. the uncontrolled use of new software.
D. the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.
translations:
34. 根据最后一段，这笔交易引发的真正担忧是
A. 科技巨头对大数据的垄断。
B. 大型制药公司之间的恶性竞争。
C. 新软件不受控制的使用。
D. 隐私法执行不力。

sentences:
35. The author’s attitude toward the application of Al to healthcare is
A. ambiguous.
B. appreciative.
C. cautious.
D. contemptuous.
translations:
35. 作者对人工智能应用于医疗保健的态度是
A. 模糊不清的。
B. 赞赏的。
C. 谨慎的。
D. 轻蔑的。
